title: Pumpkin Whoopie Pies with Cream Cheese Filling
changes_from_base: Spiced pumpkin cakes (no cocoa or buttermilk) and a cream cheese filling.
summary: This follows the classic whoopie pie method, with spiced pumpkin cakes in place of the chocolate batter (no cocoa or buttermilk) and a tangy cream cheese filling instead of vanilla buttercream.
equipment: 2 large metal baking trays lined with baking paper
stand mixer or electric hand whisk

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
full-fat cream cheese (block), at room temperature
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Preheat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) with shelves in the upper and lower thirds, allowing at least 20 minutes for it to reach temperature before baking.

steps.title: Mix the wet ingredients
steps.text: Beat the butter, oil and brown sugar together for 2 minutes, then beat in the eggs one at a time, followed by the vanilla and pumpkin purée. The oil alongside the butter helps keep these cakes moist, since pumpkin purée can otherwise make a batter feel dry.

steps.title: Fold in the spiced dry mix
steps.text: Whisk together the flour, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda, salt, cinnamon, ginger and nutmeg, then mix into the wet ingredients on low speed just until no flour is visible. Mixing only until combined keeps the crumb soft rather than dense.

steps.title: Scoop the mounds
steps.text: Scoop 24 mounds of batter onto the lined trays, spacing them 5cm apart so they have room to spread. The pumpkin batter is softer than the chocolate version, so the mounds will settle slightly as they sit.

steps.title: Bake until puffed
steps.text: Bake for 11-13 minutes, swapping the trays between shelves halfway through, until the cakes are puffed and springy to the touch. Swapping the trays keeps both batches baking at the same rate.

steps.title: Cool the cakes
steps.text: Leave the cakes on the trays for 5 minutes, then move them to a wire rack to cool completely before filling.

steps.title: Make the cream cheese frosting
steps.text: Beat the butter until smooth, then add the cream cheese and beat only until combined – overbeating cream cheese makes the frosting runny rather than firm. Add the icing sugar, vanilla and salt on low speed until smooth, then chill for 15 minutes if the mixture feels soft.

steps.title: Sandwich the pies
steps.text: Pair the cooled cakes by size and sandwich them together with a thick layer of the cream cheese filling. Store the finished pies in the fridge, where they soften further overnight – that's expected and part of their charm.

tips: Beat the cream cheese in just until combined – overbeating it makes the frosting runny instead of holding its shape.
Use tinned, unsweetened pumpkin purée rather than a very wet homemade one, as extra moisture can make the cakes spread too much.
Let the cakes cool completely before sandwiching, or the cream cheese frosting will soften too quickly.
Keep filled pies in the fridge; they turn softer overnight, which is normal here rather than a sign they've gone off.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Store filled pies in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days, as the cream cheese filling needs to stay cold. Unfilled cakes freeze for up to 2 months; thaw and fill once completely cool.
